title: Reading chromosome number and DNA amount

mc.prompt: A replicated homologous pair contains how many chromosomes and chromatids?
mc.explanation: Each of the two homologues has replicated into two chromatids.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.

mc.prompt: A 2n = 8 cell has separated sister chromatids but not completed cytokinesis. What is its whole-cell chromosome count?
mc.explanation: Separated chromatids each count as chromosomes; eight move to each pole.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.

writing.prompt: Describe the chromosome and chromatid counts in a 2n = 12 cell immediately before and immediately after S phase.
writing.model: Before S phase there are 12 unreplicated chromosomes, each with one DNA molecule. After S phase there are still 12 chromosomes but 24 sister chromatids. DNA amount has doubled without chromosome separation.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.

writing.prompt: Explain why a whole-cell count during anaphase can differ from the count in each daughter cell.
writing.model: In anaphase sister chromatids have separated into individual chromosomes, so the undivided cell contains both future chromosome groups. Cytokinesis separates these groups into two cells. Each daughter receives the original diploid chromosome number.

title: Mitosis: chromosome movement through the stages

mc.answer: New nuclei form around chromosome groups at opposite poles
mc.explanation: Telophase reorganizes nuclei after chromosome separation.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Tetrads cross over at the cell equator
Gametes fuse to form a zygote
New nuclei form around chromosome groups at opposite poles
DNA is being replicated in an intact interphase nucleus

mc.prompt: Why is attachment of sister chromatids to opposite poles important?
mc.answer: It supports delivery of one replicated copy to each daughter nucleus
mc.explanation: Opposite-pole attachment helps distribute copied chromosomes accurately.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: It creates alleles needed by the organism
It halves chromosome number in every body cell
It ensures one daughter receives only maternal chromosomes
It supports delivery of one replicated copy to each daughter nucleus

writing.prompt: Trace chromosome behaviour through the four stages of mitosis.
writing.model: In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle becomes organized. In metaphase replicated chromosomes align individually at the equator. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. In telophase nuclei reform around the chromosome groups as chromosomes become less condensed.

writing.prompt: Contrast what separates in mitosis with the separation of a maternal and paternal homologue.
writing.model: Mitosis separates sister chromatids, the replicated copies of one chromosome. A maternal and paternal chromosome are homologues, not sister chromatids. Their separation as intact replicated chromosomes occurs in meiosis I, which reduces chromosome sets.
